newsitem.title: KENYA: Summit on Zaire urges deployment of neutral force.
newsitem.headline: Summit on Zaire urges deployment of neutral force.

text.p: African leaders called on Tuesday for a neutral force to deploy urgently in eastern Zaire with U.N. Security Council approval to protect more than a million refugees.
The call was in a final statement read out in front of the leaders in Nairobi by Kenyan Foreign Minister Kalonzo Musyoka.
"The summit called for the immediate setting up of safe corridors and temporary sanctuaries inside Zaire to facilitate humanitarian assistance and the repatriation of refugees," he said.
"The summit requested the U.N. Security Council to take urgent measures to ensure the establishment of the safe corridors and temporary sanctuaries by deploying a neutral force," he added.

He said the summit, which however was not attended by any Zairean representative, called on U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali and Organisation of African Unity (OAU) Secretary-General Salim Ahmed Salim to coordinate on the move.
"The summit...agreed that an immediate ceasefire should be effected and strictly observed," said Musyoka, adding that it also "reaffirmed its commitment to the territorial integrity of Zaire".
The leaders urged intensified efforts for the voluntary repatriation of refugees to Rwanda and called for implementation of a long-standing decision to separate "intimidators" from refugees.
In a reference to Banyamulenge Tutsis who have seized much of eastern Zaire in a two-week-old offensive, they confirmed the rights of minorities to be considered as citizens.
The Banyamulenge arrived in what is now Zaire from what is now Rwanda as long ago as 200 years ago but were denied Zairean citizenship in 1981.

The presidents of Kenya, Eritrea, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zambia and the prime minister of Ethiopia attended the Nairobi talks on Africa's most serious crisis since the 1994 genocide of Tutsis in Rwanda in the same "Great Lakes" region.
Zaire, which accuses Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda of sending troops into its territory to fight alongside the rebels, said it would not attend any talks on the crisis until foreign troops withdrew.
OAU chief Salim, the foreign minister of the current OAU chairman Cameroon and elder statesman Julius Nyerere also took part in the one-day summit at State House in the Kenyan capital.
